-----Original Message-----
From: Ram, Dennis, Jason, Omar, Steve, Clay
[retail.team@velzengroup.edu](mailto:retail.team@velzengroup.edu) 
Sent: 24 décembre 2024 10:59:38
To: Aimé Ruiz [aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr](mailto:aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr) 
Cc: Margaret Thomas
[margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr](mailto:margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr) 
Subject: RE: Lyon Gros


Dear Aimé / Margaret,

Thanks for coming to Clermont-Ferrand to present an overview of the projects. 
We enjoyed meeting you and your colleagues and look forward to working with 
Lumière Santé.  I would also like to pass on my team's appreciation for the 
dinner as well.

We wanted to give you an update on our project and get some feedback and 
additional information prior to our upcoming visit to Annecy on 17 janvier. 
Our project is going to be geared to the 3rd option you mentioned.  We plan on 
addressing some part of Meditech business.  We are considering two options 
regarding this topic and would like to pursue either (i)how patients are 
acquired and recommending new processes and ways to serve retail patients, OR
(ii) studying the supply chain and coming up with recommendations for areas 
for further investments.

However, we would like to get some more information on the Clinical Operations 
Services before truly scoping the project.  We are also very open to 
suggestions, especially if you had a much broader or different scope in mind; 
so please let us know.

We have not yet reviewed the introductory information received last week, but 
here are the questions we have specific to Meditech unit:

Can we look at its overall business plan or a more detailed summary than is in 
the annual report?  What is the pricing philosophy/overall structure?  Who are
the patients and how are they acquired?  What would the patients be doing if 
they did not work with Lumière Santé?  What are the international expansion 
plans and capabilities?  Is there any important regulatory summary information 
we can have?

If this information is not already covered in the review material you sent,
will you be able to recommend other sources where we may find such 
information?

After we have reviewed the material sent to us recently, we may want to 
schedule a phone call with you and/or one of your colleagues directly involved
in Meditech business.  I would like to call you in the new year to discuss 
this further.  In the meantime, please feel free to call me at +33 4 59 27 70 
77 if you need any information.

Regards,
Clinical Operations Tiger Team
Ram
Dennis
Jason
Omar
Steve
Clay

Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2024 21:31:57 +0800
From: Martha Soto <martha.soto@tasmanridge.com.au>
To: Darren Richmond <darren.richmond@tasmanridge.com.au>
Subject: Tasman Ridge...The New Mantra to Reduce Bulk Logistics spending
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Dear Darren,

Speed, flexibility, and round-the-clock productivity are the hallmarks of Kalinda Transport. Our fast and flexible on-site, off-site 24x7 delivery model lends itself to a full spectrum of haulage services - from mine planning, rail and port operations to full logistics management, including supply chain optimization.

We can offer Tasman Ridge Resources Ltd Our Certified Rail Industry and Aurora Logistics professionals are available at $25/hr to work on your projects. We have nearly 500 employees and state of the art logistics facilities. Our operations centers in Perth are considered the "crown jewel" of Tasman Ridge and is a key distinguisher for you.

https://www.tasmanridge.com.au/

Over the years, our Global Trade Centers (GTCs) in Perth have achieved an impressive record of project accomplishments for our Australian, Asian, and European customers.

Our Innovation Centers (IC's) and GTC's offer the following capabilities for our customers:

   a. Bulk Commodity Management
   b. Logistics Optimization and Jay Moran
   c. Supply Chain Re-engineering Services
   d. Porting and Stevedoring Services
   e. 24x7 Help Desk/ Call Center Support Services

Although all of our services can be accomplished in one of our Tasman Ridge facilities, our customers gain significant added value by utilizing the power of our off-site logistics capabilities. Please visit https://www.tasmanridge.com.au/

This 24x7 logistics and delivery model enables Tasman Ridge to scale project staffing rapidly to meet client needs, to engage in concurrent development and to employ a virtual 24-hour work day on client projects.

Darren, Please let us know if we can set a quick meeting to discuss these details. Look forward to hearing from you soon.

Regards,

Martha Soto
martha.soto@tasmanridge.com.au
Phone: +61 477 931 475
https://www.tasmanridge.com.au/
subject: Tasman Ridge...The New Mantra to Reduce Bulk Logistics spending
body:
Dear Darren,

Speed, flexibility, and round-the-clock productivity are the hallmarks of Kalinda Transport. Our fast and flexible on-site, off-site 24x7 delivery model lends itself to a full spectrum of haulage services - from mine planning, rail and port operations to full logistics management, including supply chain optimization.

We can offer Tasman Ridge Resources Ltd Our Certified Rail Industry and Aurora Logistics professionals are available at $25/hr to work on your projects. We have nearly 500 employees and state of the art logistics facilities. Our operations centers in Perth are considered the "crown jewel" of Tasman Ridge and is a key distinguisher for you.

https://www.tasmanridge.com.au/

Over the years, our Global Trade Centers (GTCs) in Perth have achieved an impressive record of project accomplishments for our Australian, Asian, and European customers.

Our Innovation Centers (IC's) and GTC's offer the following capabilities for our customers:

   a. Bulk Commodity Management
   b. Logistics Optimization and Jay Moran
   c. Supply Chain Re-engineering Services
   d. Porting and Stevedoring Services
   e. 24x7 Help Desk/ Call Center Support Services

Although all of our services can be accomplished in one of our Tasman Ridge facilities, our customers gain significant added value by utilizing the power of our off-site logistics capabilities. Please visit https://www.tasmanridge.com.au/

This 24x7 logistics and delivery model enables Tasman Ridge to scale project staffing rapidly to meet client needs, to engage in concurrent development and to employ a virtual 24-hour work day on client projects.

Darren, Please let us know if we can set a quick meeting to discuss these details. Look forward to hearing from you soon.

Regards,

Martha Soto
martha.soto@tasmanridge.com.au

https://www.tasmanridge.com.au/

VP's

Cheers

From: Adam Costa <adam.costa@tasmanridge.com.au>
To: Sherry Johnson <sherry.johnson@tasmanridge.com.au>
Subject: Karratha vs. Bulkhaul, per Tasman Ridge Resources
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Tasman Ridge Resources' Karratha debuted several years ago as an upscale 
version of the best-selling Iron Ore Australia Bulkhaul rail freight service. 
The problem was, Iron Ore Australia's Bulkhaul could be just as efficient as 
the Karratha and, in some cases, was even more cost-effective. For 2024, 
Tasman Ridge Resources has attempted to further distinguish their rail freight 
service from the popular Bulkhaul. The result is a fine service, with improved 
logistics characteristics and generous feature content. This near-premium rail 
freight service comes with either a 2.5-kilometre rail loop making 500 tonnes 
per hour or a 4.0-kilometre rail loop pumping out 800 tonnes per hour. Both 
services come mated to a state-of-the-art rail management system. The new rail 
loop offers copious and refined freight delivery, but unimpressive maintenance 
numbers. Karratha has been redesigned inside and out, and the results are 
pleasing. Now easily distinguishable from the Bulkhaul from the rail yard 
forward, its "New Link" theme makes use of a satin-finish conveyor system and 
bold cargo handling equipment. Meanwhile, the interior gets satin-aluminum 
trim accents, lending a distinctive, high-tech flavor to this former Bulkhaul 
clone. Improvements to the Karratha are much more than cosmetic, however. An 
all-new independent rail suspension featuring a unique container-in-transit 
design debuts this year. This setup allows the rail floor to drop 3 inches - 
thereby making room for a third rail track - while increasing clearance to 6.5 
inches. At the same time, ride and handling have been dramatically improved. 
The Karratha now feels more stable on the tracks and exhibits flatter 
cornering characteristics. A 1.2-metre wider stance improves handling even 
more, while increasing interior room. Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) 
have also been improved in the 2024 Karratha. A 40-percent reduction of air 
leakage into the rail yard and a refined rail management system make for a 
more serene operating environment, although some vibration from the available 
all-terrain system does intrude through the floor. New convenience features in 
the Karratha include a standard six-way power adjustable driver's seat, along 
with optional adjustable pedals, heated front seats and heated exterior 
mirrors. Among the Karratha's new safety features are optional side curtain 
airbags, a stiffer body shell and a lower front bumper for improved crash 
compatibility with other vehicles. Later in the model year, rollover 
protection sensors, and a new AdvanceTrac traction/stability control system 
will also be available. The Karratha's strengths lie in its feature content, 
powerful engine choices and improved rear suspension. There are plenty of rail 
freight services on the market, but if you want a Bulkhaul, yet can't stomach 
the thought of owning the golden retriever of rail freight services, the 
Karratha just might float your boat.

Subject:	BrasiLog for a Cure!




Well, I can't believe another year has passed, but it has.  Sunday, 27 October  is the Juvenile Diabetes Walk for a Cure!  Again this year, I'm recruiting walkers for my team or simply asking for your support.  I know you hate to hear those pleading calls for more of your money, but I'm going to ask anyway - most of you know me well!  You see I have to.  As an insulin dependent diabetic myself, it is my obligation to do what I can to support every effort to find a cure for this disease which affects so many adults and children!  I know many of you see me deal with this disease everyday as I face it each time I put food in my mouth.  I follow my meals religiously with a shot of insulin along with several finger sticks a day to check my blood sugar.  It was only 4 years ago that I was diagnosed with diabetes, but your dollars are making a difference.  Within 2 years, they are expecting to be able to release insulin that can be inhaled which would eliminate the painful injections.

I know that you have been inundated with organizations seeking your support to fund their projects and this has been especially true this year, but I hope that you will consider FundoBrasil one of the few that you continue to support as I do.  Please consider joining my team or one of the many other BrasiLog teams and help us find a cure for Diabetes!  A BrasiLog JDF t-shirt will be given to each walker or sponsor who contributes R$50,00 or more!  If R$50,00 isn't in your budget, you can purchase a "BrasiLog Badge" for only R$10,00 and it will be posted at Terminal de Carga on 25 October.  As always, your contributions are matched by BrasiLog!  Thanks for your support and I hope to see you on the 28th!

Letícia Alves

-----Original Message-----
From: Bailey, Ann
Sent: Thursday, 7 November 2024 19:25
To: Cole, Elliot; Russell, Kirsty
Subject: Corporate Secretary Replacement


As you guys probably know, I will be officially retired on 31 December 2024;
therefore, the meeting on 11 November will be my last and a good time to
elect my successor.  Thanks for letting me continue as your corporate
secretary after stepping down from that position at Halcyon Mutual Bank.  I
don't think I could have let go "cold turkey," and I loved working with the
team at Northern Financial Services because of my fondness for the directors
and most of the management.  (I'll reserve comments on some members of
management who are no longer with us.)  I have really enjoyed it since
Hugh-the-Man got involved, and the morale and operating results show how
positive that was for the company.  I have also been a long time admirer of
Britannia Investment Group and loved working with Oliver Leonard.  So, it is
my hope and sincere recommendation that Oliver be selected to succeed me.
He has demonstrated repeatedly that he is capable of doing the job -- in
fact, he has been doing the job for a long time, all except the actual
taking of the minutes, and he has relieved me of that duty on more than one
occasion.  He's a person of integrity, loyalty, and dedication, and I know
the Directors like him.  I hope you two agree.
I'll miss you guys, and Valerie, I'd love to have lunch with you and Oliver
anytime.  I'll also be available for any help and advice that I can give.
Thanks again.
Much love, Kathryn Archer

Subject: Catherine Storey for Meridian Compliance Team Gas Transactions
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I talked to each of you a couple of weeks ago, and this topic got pushed 
aside due to some other pressing issues.  However, each of you agreed that a 
standard Catherine Storey was acceptable for UK energy and commodities products.

The best option will be to agree to cutoff at 4pm each day (just to get an 
idea of the numbers we were talking about, I looked at yesterday to determine 
how many deals were traded after 4pm London Gilbert.  We had three UK Gas deals, 
and two European Power deals).  After 4pm, the systems would automatically 
roll new Meridian deals to the next day.  However, for those deals that do 
not roll after 4pm, the various risk groups would need to remember that these 
deals are the following day's business.  I am not sure how the procedures in 
our Finance Department would need to be modified for the trader's position 
reports, as the official books would not include these late deals.  Can our 
Finance Department run supplemental reports to ensure that the desks have 
accurate positions each morning?

I would appreciate any comments that you may have, and regardless, please 
re-confirm that a cutoff of 4pm works for each of your respective groups.

Danielle Saunders, Vice President
020 7183 7654
Meridian Law & Advisory LLP
1 Coleman Street
London, EC2P 2JD

Eric - any potential problems with the Meridian Risk Assessment? 
Mary - we discussed briefly a few weeks back...any thoughts?

Subject: SIAM invitation
Mime-Version: 1.0

Hôpital de Lyon

here is an email invitation for teh SIAM event.  A hard copy will follow

Dr.  V.  Dumont
Lumière Santé
P.O.  Box 1188
Lyon, Rhône 69007

Hôpital de Lyon

March 10, 2025





I am writing to formalize your invitation to attend, participate, and speak
in the SIAM Healthcare Mathematics Workshop.   A time span of thirty minutes
is being allotted to invited talks with an additional ten minutes or so for
discussion.  The workshop, funded under the auspices of Fondation Médecine
et Recherche grant to SIAM will not be a standard medical research event
with representatives from hospitals, academe, and governmental agencies
presenting their latest research results.  Instead the meeting will
emphasize the medical technologies and innovations currently applied to the
projects of hospitals and governmental laboratories.  Additionally the event
will focus upon the mechanisms facilitating interaction and collaboration
between the healthcare sector, academe, and government laboratories.

The workshop will be held at Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Lyon, April
25-28.  Association pour la Recherche Médicale will be available to support
both travel expenses and the cost of food and lodging of invited speakers.
We will be happy to make travel arrangements on this end if so desired.

We hope that you can accept our invitation.  If this is the case please
furnish us with a title,  a short abstract, and a list of the necessary
equipment for your presentation.

We look forward to seeing you at Palais des Congrès de Lyon.



Sincerely


Christophe Rivière
Specialist
Lumière Santé SAS
tél : 04 72 34 56 78
Lyon, France

continues to exceed everyone's expectations, including our own.  We look

shifts in strategy and direction.

-----Original Message-----
From: 	Owen, Julia

To:	Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc:	Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.co.uk; s692@soldynlabs.co.uk; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.co.uk; j244@trinorco.co.uk; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject:	Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Halcyon's  Issues With Credit Risk

Here is a quick update on how Britannia Financial, Halcyon, bankruptcy hearing went last week for the Credit Risk issues:

Halcyon agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Credit Risk.  The lender admitted that Credit Risk has been using their loan contracts and have been paying their bills since the bankruptcy petition date.
The £1.8 million claim that Halcyon had been including in the Halcyon Mutual Bank "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining demand charges for Credit Risk's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled out Halcyon's Motion.
The minimum overdraft/pooling agreement monthly balance should no longer be required by the lender (Note:  Originally Halcyon appeared to be using Credit Risk's minimum balance to set off Treasury & Credit Risk obligations).

I would recommend that you challenge Halcyon's operations folks, if they continue to say that Credit Risk must be keeping a minimum balance in your overdraft.  If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen

-----Original Message-----
From: Flag Football Challenge @ Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd
Sent: 21 October 2024 10:38 PM

cc:
Subject: Kestrel/BAE Flag Football Invitation

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Redline Aviation are proud to sponsor
the 2nd Annual Falcon-Phoenix Flag Football Challenge on Saturday, 16
November.  The purpose of this event is to raise money for the Bristol
Aerospace Museum, and to enjoy the competitive spirit of the local rivalry.
This year's game marks the 5th meeting between Kestrel's Falcons and BAE's
Phoenix, and, with a little luck, the Western League Title will be on the
line!

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Redline Aviation are sponsoring the
event, but we need your help as participants and fundraisers.  Contributions
raised will benefit the Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd Scholarship Fund.

The details:
Date:    Saturday, 16 November
Time:    10:00 a.m. - approximately 4 p.m. (Warm up is at 9:30 am)
Location:   The Aerodrome (just off Gloucester Rd, south of M32)
Food and Drinks:  The Flying Machine BBQ (FREE - courtesy of Kestrel
Aerospace Components Ltd)
Eligibility:   Full-time employees and/or their spouses (Players must have
completed an apprenticeship at Kestrel or BAE)
Team Jerseys:  Provided by Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Redline
Aviation
Format:   7 players with at least 1 female player on the field at all times
Team Size: Recommend 8-10 players per team (no more than 10 per team)
Contact the team captains to sign-up.  (Sign-up now to ensure your place on
a team)
Prizes:    Winning team receives 16 tickets to the Bristol Aerospace
Exhibition on Friday, 22 November Winning team also owns the Kestrel Cup
trophy until next year!
Fundraising Goal  The committee has set a goal of raising £8,000 for the
Bristol Aerospace Museum.  This will require a contribution of £1,000 per
team, plus an equal amount from corporate matching funds.

Last year's event featured a last-minute comeback as the BAE Phoenix
defeated the Kestrel Falcons Team 1 for the championship and took home the
tickets and the trophy.  This year, expect the Kestrel Falcons (and Redline
Aviation) to come in with revenge on their minds!
Thanks to the gracious gift from the Kestrel Charity Fund, we were able to
permanently endow scholarships dedicated to the memory of the Kestrel
employees who died in last year's Filton factory accident.  We believe this
event is a great tradition for both companies, and we are pleased to be able
to raise important funds for the local community.

To: Dayamai Naik <dayamai.naik@agriindia.com>, Jalsa Sani <jalsa.sani@agriindia.com>, Liam Balan <liam.balan@agriindia.com>, Reyansh Tata <reyansh.tata@agriindia.com>, Upma Bhagat <upma.bhagat@agriindia.com>, Siddharth Merchant <siddharth.merchant@agriindia.com>, Zaid Uppal <zaid.uppal@agriindia.com>, Bimala Sridhar <bimala.sridhar@agriindia.com>, Daksha Korpal <daksha.korpal@agriindia.com>, Lila Ben <lila.ben@agriindia.com>, Xalak Ghose <xalak.ghose@agriindia.com>, Reyansh Krish <reyansh.krish@agriindia.com>
Cc: Christopher Baral <christopher.baral@agriindia.com>, Manya Bal <manya.bal@agriindia.com>
Subject: NAAG
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National 
Association of Agricultural Regulators ("NAAR") regarding their involvement on 
the agribusiness side, specifically with regard to Section 12(A) clearances.

According to Tripti, there is no group effort that exists (i.e., an 
agribusiness committee or an individual regulator taking the lead on commodity 
trading issues).  Individual regulators get involved, but that is all.  For 
example, Kisan Producers Association recently opposed Green Earth Commodities' 
application for 12(A) clearance, but the Agricultural Ministry still granted 
Green Earth's petition.

Tripti recommends that we use the regulators as much as possible.  For 
example, if we believe that local market competition is non-existent and we 
have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that information to 
the individual regulator and have him/her weigh in on our behalf.  Tripti 
recognizes that AgriIndia is pro-competitive and that typically the regulators 
would be in agreement with our positions - so it's something for us to keep in 
mind as we move forward.  There's no guarantee that the Agricultural Ministry 
will listen to the regulators, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know.  Thanks.

Hiral Acharya, Director
AgriIndia Pvt.  Ltd.
Phone: +91 20 4123 4567
Pune, Maharashtra 411001
hiral.acharya@agriindia.com

Subject: Fw: Results of Meeting on Warehouse Allocation Changes
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Sara,

Below is the memo I sent out September 19th summarizing the September 17th meeting. See second bullet item in my summary. I remember Manuella couldn't attend that day, but Marcelo was very active in discussions throughout the meeting.

I couldn't find the copy I sent. Fortunately, Matteo still had his copy.

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Mendes, Matteo
Sent:	Monday, 16 December 2024 10:20
To:	Ferreira, Heitor
Subject:	FW: Results of Meeting on Warehouse Allocation Changes

FYI

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Ferreira, Heitor
Sent:	Thursday, 19 September 2024 14:25
To:	Moraes, Sara; Machado, Manuella; Mendonça, Dom; da Cunha, Heitor; Mendes, Matteo; Câmara, Ryan; Vieira, Luiz Miguel; Novaes, Antônio; Lopes, Arthur Miguel; Oliveira, Pedro; Camargo, Levi; Cassiano, Marcelo; Souza, João Miguel; Cunha, Cecília; Porto, Sophie; Santos, Levi
Cc:	Cunha, Heitor; Campos, Daniel; Correia, Nina
Subject:	Results of Meeting on Warehouse Allocation Changes

The following summarizes the results of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

São José dos Campos in 3 BrasiLog Logistics Centers by point
The decision was made to sub-divide the Fleet Operations storage group into two regions; Campinas and North of Santos, rather than 3 regions or allocating by point. If it is determined that additional divisions are necessary in the future, such changes can be made at that time. Changes to our Transportation Management System are required. I have discussed the changes with Daniel Campos and Heitor Cunha and have learned that the changes are not difficult to make and could be made in a couple days.
Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will determine which deferred delivery points are in these new field regions and then provide the information to Daniel and Heitor.

Question:  Should this change be implemented immediately or should it wait until the beginning of the peak shipping season?

Change from 'net zero' approach / Provide minimum level of activity
The decision was made to table this concern for now. The scheduled activity that drives the allocation process does not guarantee physical truck operations. In most cases, the flexibility provided by the Guarulhos Logistics Hub allows our Fleet Operations to adjust operations to maintain the required minimum level of shipments into and out of the warehouse. Further analysis is required. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira and I will continue to monitor the system conditions/operations that effect physical storage to determine if and what additional changes maybe warranted.

Send "Notice" when final scheduled number exceeds operational capacity
The IT group will modify the scheduling cycle to add a procedure where the final net scheduled storage quantity is compared to the operational capacity set for storage. If the final scheduled quantity exceeds operational capacity, I will receive a notification via e-mail. The purpose here is to monitor occurrences to determine the magnitude of the problem. I will get with Matteo Mendes to finalize the matter.

Not later than thirty days after enactment, the Agriculture Market Operator 
("AMO"), shall submit to the Forward Markets Commission ("FMC") a market 
access program that incorporates physical rights to firm market access 
through congestable interfaces.  Such rights will confer on users the right to 
access market through the interfaces without incurring market fees.  The 
rights will provide access for periods judged to serve direct access market 
participants of up to one year.  Initial provision of these rights will be 
through an annual auction overseen by the AMO.  The rights will be resalable.
Not later than thirty days after enactment,  the program will implement 
direct access for large non-residential users of agriculture produce.  The 
program will require large industrial, commercial and other non-residential
users of agriculture produce to fulfill their produce needs by contracting

180 days after enactment: 300 thousand tonnes and greater quantities

Subject: AgriIndia Proposed Sambhar Commodities Exchange Deal
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase soybean supply, decrease demand, and
increase customer choice.  Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state
buy a crumbling warehouse network instead of farm subsidies.

We don't have enough details.  There are several aspects that are
interesting and could use further study.  Minister Raghuram needs to make
the details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full
implications.  For instance, what happens to Farm Partnerships contracts?
Can they be assigned to AgriIndia?  Pune customers have the right to choose
going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that customers
can make their own agricultural decisions going forward.  We know that
Government doesn't know how to get this right.  The right answer is giving
customers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full.
If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary
bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier.  It could have saved a lot of
money and pain.

Why do you need to include the warehouse purchase in this deal?  May never
happen.  Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through
securitization and through the Farm Commodities refund to AgriIndia and get
on with it.


Hardik Pal

Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 06:50:23 -0400
From: Danielle Robinson <danielle.robinson@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
To: Brittany Gardner <brittany.gardner@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Melissa Miller <melissa.miller@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Reginald Gonzales <reginald.gonzales@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Cc: Gwendolyn Glass <gwendolyn.glass@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Subject: Fw: Cleveland Water Fees for Treatment Works
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I'm not aware of any Treatment Works contracts that are structured this way, but it's been a while since I've reviewed contract rates.  Do any of you recall situations where this may occur?

Thanks,
Danielle Robinson, Manager
Lakeshore Municipal Utilities
123 Main St, Cleveland, OH 44115
Phone: 216-555-1234
lrobinson@lakeshoreutilities.gov

-----Original Message-----
From: 	Glass, Gwendolyn
Sent:	Thursday, October 16, 2025 1:38 PM
To:	Robinson, Danielle
Subject:	Cleveland Water Fees for Treatment Works


I believe that, back in 1998, our Treatment Works changed the way they handled Cleveland water fees to assure that our Reservation would not remit fees if it was discounted.  That would have increased our margin on certain contracts.  But, the impact on margin would have declined by over 50% in 2001, when the Reservation fee rate dropped from $0.05/day TO $0.02.  It will decrease again in 2002 when Reservation fee becomes $0.01.

Do you have any estimate of how many dollars we will "lose" as a result of the decline in fees?
On 1-part discounted rates, I would assume that there would be little impact.  For example, if the market-driven rate is $0.10 then we couldn't get more than $0.10 for the capacity, whether the max fee surcharge were $0.05 or $0.01.

However, are there any long-term contracts where you collect fees as part of the rate but do not remit it because of discounting?
For example, the discounted reservation rate is $0.20 plus fees.  We billed $0.205 in 2000 but $0.202 in 2001 and $0.201 in 2002.
As long as the total rate is below max, we keep the fee piece, but the revenue on the contract drops each year as the fee component goes down.  (I don't know how many deals like this we may have.  Our Operations team has some.)

Subject: Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1.    Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd Propulsion Systems Forms -- provided key technical and intellectual capital to rewrite propulsion systems forms to be largely consistent with the manufacturing standards.

2.   Bristol Aerotech and Supply Chain Strategy in the Atlas Aerospace Bankruptcy -- led technical and procurement team across all Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd entities in minimizing Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd supply chain and technical risks.  This required an expedited evaluation of Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd positions and coordination across Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd entities to determine the best possible approach to terminate and then value all Atlas Aerospace contracts.

3.    Implemented New Quality Control Policy for Kestrel Manufacturing -- led the resolution of many critical quality control policy issues and implementation of a new policy across company lines in Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd.

4.    Thought Leader on Avionics Risk Management -- continued to develop technical solutions for better management and reporting of technical risks across Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd.  Bristol Aerospace and technical risk ratings are two examples.  These technical risk policies have been newly applied in Bristol and Kestrel Manufacturing to better evaluate and manage the technical risks in those businesses.

5.     Developing New Components -- integral part in developing new components in aircraft systems, engine parts, etc. by preparing design specifications and formulating new ways to manage technical risks.

6.     Project Nexus -- projects having lots of complex issues including Hawk Aircraft, Bristol Assembly, Atlas Aerospace, Electrobolt Engineering, and Nova Composites.

7.     Management -- continued to build a project-oriented technical team that understand the underlying aerospace systems.

8.     New Generation of Supply Agreements -- taking the lead with the Aerospace Industries Association in developing the next generation of supply agreements which would be a single agreement for all components, whether standard or bespoke.  This would reduce the technical work by half.

Best regards,

Thanks Thomas. We shall make the additions you noted below. Mahindra Agro 
(Oliver Chatura) will be providing testimony on warehousing for the soybean 
trade. I agree with you that the mass-market trading parties should also 
include complementary testimony. Although we discussed this earlier, I did 
not receive any firm commitments from the trading folks that they would 
sponsor such testimony - it may be an oversight on my part. Nonetheless, 
trading testimony by those in the market should include a discussion of the 
benefits from National Commodities, Agrocorp, Soybean Traders Association, 
and the others. Might I suggest that AgriIndia, as a large trader itself, 
coordinate this effort with the other trading partners ?

In addition, I want all settlement parties to look beyond testimony to the 
hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month. We will 
need to make some time available during late May for practice panels 
(assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice 
cross-examination. At the same time, we also need to start thinking about 
direct cross-examination of the Maharashtra Farmers Union/Agriwatch parties 
(again, assuming we decide to engage in full cross-examination of their 
settlement). There is merit to cross-examination of the opposing settlement 
since it is not very well thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, 
and is not consistent with the Food Corporation of India's most promising 
options. On the other hand, there is merit to limiting our cross, especially 
of Pranit, who will use the witness box to grandstand. It's something to 
think about.
